key_insight: A training-free, knowledge-graph-based diagnostic framework can map patient observations to explicit medical ontology rules and rank candidate diseases without learning from outcome labels.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support auditable, explainable decision support by separating evidence matching, clustering, and rule-based diagnosis from supervised prediction.
method: Builds candidate-specific evidence feature nodes from patient observations and medical knowledge.
Uses a bounded information gate, knowledge-weighted evidence accumulation, disease similarity, and clinical rules to rank diagnoses.
Clusters cases with label-free K-means on four derived evidence coordinates rather than raw predictors or outcomes.
evidence_signal: Across six retrospective cohorts, the label-free protocol reported positive-class F1 scores ranging from 0.634 to 0.996 and full partition-decision coverage, with logistic regression used as a supervised baseline.
watch_item: Retrospective results do not establish prospective clinical validity, and influenza cases included confirmatory PCR rather than independent pre-test prediction.
paper_title: Training-Free Clinical Reasoning through Medical Ontologies and Cognitive Mapping: A Symbolic-Probabilistic Knowledge Graph Framework
